newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI announces norms for satellite dealers.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI announces norms for satellite dealers.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Tuesday subsidiaries of commercial banks or financial institutions or companies incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956 were eligible to apply for registration as satellite dealers in government securities.
Satellite dealers would form a second rung in the government securities market after primary dealers.

"They are expected to further strengthen the infrastructure in the government securities market, enhance liquidity and turnover (in government securities) and provide a retail outlet (for government securities), thereby encouraging voluntary holding (of government securities) among a wider investor base," the RBI said in a statement.
It said applicants for satellite dealership would need to have minimum net owned funds of 50 million rupees.
They would also have to enter into an arrangement with the RBI to generate outright turnover in central government securities, including treasury bills, of not less than 300 million rupees in a year.
Satellite dealers would be required to achieve an annual turnover of not less than five times in government securities, including treasury bills, the RBI said.

They would have to achieve a portfolio of not less than 20 percent in government securities in relation to total assets before the end of the first year of operations after registration and to maintain prescribed capital adequacy standards, the RBI added.

It said it would extend facilities such as current account and subsidiary general ledger account to satellite dealers and allow them to borrow and lend in the money market, including the call money market.
It said it would recommend to the central government that the facility of ready forward transactions be extended to satellite dealers.
